Command: The robe's hem shall not be torn
Summary: The command: The robe's hem shall not be torn (Exodus 28:32). The ephod's robe was woven whole, with its opening bound so that it would not tear.
Commandment: The robe's hem shall not be torn.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: The robe was woven whole, its opening bound so it would not tear — a ceremonial law in a single stitch. Its goal was to keep the high priest's garment intact in service, the wholeness of the robe matching the wholeness of the office. Scripture gives no particular evil this restrained, and I will not invent one; its work was order and reverence, not restraint. A torn robe would have been a torn sign; the binding kept the garment, and what it signified, unbroken.
